summary: The National Quantum Initiative Reauthorization Act reauthorizes and expands federal programs supporting quantum information science, engineering, and technology. It extends the timeline of the initiative, expands agency coordination, authorizes new research centers, testbeds, and educational hubs, and establishes strict research security requirements.

affected_groups.effect: Gain access to expanded STEM and quantum-focused fellowships, scholarships, traineeships, research experiences, and curriculum development resources across K-12, undergraduate, and graduate levels.
Eligible to compete for federal grants and awards to establish quantum research centers, acceleration centers, testbeds, and the QREW Coordination Hub.
affected_groups.group: Institutions of Higher Education and Nonprofits

affected_groups.effect: Industry participants, small- and medium-sized businesses, and startups are integrated into public-private partnerships, supply chain efforts, testbeds, and advisory committees to promote commercialization.
Multiple federal agencies—including NIST, NSF, DOE, and NASA—are assigned expanded roles in quantum research coordination, infrastructure development, and use-case identification.

key_provisions: Reauthorizes the National Quantum Initiative Act through December 30, 2032.

Expands the National Science Foundation's programs to include student traineeships, fellowships, scholarships, K-12 educator professional learning, and a Quantum Reskilling, Education, and Workforce (QREW) Coordination Hub.

Authorizes the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to establish quantum acceleration centers, carry out post-quantum cryptography deployment and grant programs, and create an international quantum research program.

Directs the Department of Energy to operate National Quantum Information Science Research Centers, establish a quantum instrumentation and foundry program, and conduct research to enhance the security and resilience of the electric grid.
Authorizes NASA to carry out quantum research and establish a NASA Quantum Institute for space and aeronautics applications.

Requires the Office of Science and Technology Policy to submit an International Quantum Cooperation Strategy and establishes a Subcommittee on the Economic and Security Implications of Quantum Information Science.

Prohibits the use of authorized funds by higher education institutions maintaining contracts with Confucius Institutes and restricts joint quantum research activities with foreign countries or entities of concern.
missing_information: Specific funding authorization amounts and dollar figures for the reauthorized programs and new initiatives are not provided in the text.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The National Quantum Initiative Reauthorization Act reauthorizes and expands federal programs supporting quantum information science, engineering, and technology. It extends the timeline of the initiative, expands agency coordination, authorizes new research centers, testbeds, and educational hubs, and establishes strict research security requirements.
summary_detail.significance: The legislation significantly broadens the scope of federal involvement in quantum technology by scaling up multi-agency research, establishing dedicated national testbeds and foundries, investing heavily in domestic workforce pathways, and incorporating rigorous international cooperation and research security measures.
